The server decides
where every car is.

ApexSim runs a 240 Hz authoritative physics simulation in Rust and renders it in Unreal Engine 5. Seventeen cars, twenty-six real circuits, and no second physics model to argue with.

What's under the bodywork

Built like
a race car

Every system that matters to how a car drives lives on the server, computed from the tyres outward. The client's job is to render it faithfully and get out of the way.

01 / PHYSICS

A four-wheel model that earns its grip

Per-wheel loads, Pacejka-style tyres, suspension, a drivetrain with per-gear ratios, and front and rear aero that feeds real downforce into the wheel loads. Deterministic to the bit, guarded by a test that asserts identical runs.

  • Pacejka tyres
  • Aero balance
  • Tyre pressure
  • Deterministic
02 / NETCODE

One simulation, clocked in server ticks

TCP+TLS for the lobby, UDP for telemetry and input, bound by a token handshake. Cars are rendered from a telemetry buffer interpolated between samples and dead-reckoned across gaps, so motion stays smooth without a second model to reconcile.

  • Protocol v2
  • MessagePack
  • ~60% smaller wire
  • Prometheus metrics
03 / CIRCUITS

Real ground, real furniture

Measured centerlines, per-side width, banking and elevation from Copernicus GLO-30. Stands, pit lanes, barriers and woodland laid from OpenStreetMap dossiers.

04 / FORCE FEEDBACK

Feel the front let go

Steering-column torque summed from each front tyre's aligning moment, scrub and jacking. The rim goes light at the grip peak, just like the real thing. DirectInput wheels, pedals and button boxes.

05 / AUDIO

Engines that are simulated, not sampled

A crank turned at live RPM fires each cylinder into exhaust banks, headers and a silencer. Crossplane burble, overrun pops, gear whine. Zero audio files.

06 / WEATHER

Rain and the clock

Five weather states and any time of day. Wet grip is baked into the session, so physics, AI and the racing line all follow. Floodlights and headlights come on after dark.

07 / HOTLAP

Garage, ghost, repeat

Time attack with sector splits, track limits and records that persist. Chase your best lap's ghost, replay it from the TV cameras, then tune 14 setup knobs.

08 / RACECRAFT

AI and a TV director

Deterministic AI drivers with a traffic layer. Behind the menus, a broadcast director follows battles through trackside, helicopter and onboard shots.

The grid

17 cars.
Four classes.

Every car is a physics definition and a 3D model, shared verbatim between the server, the track editor and the client. The AI fills the field from your car's own class.

Paint shop

Every car, three ways

Liveries repaint paint, accent and logo at runtime on the race car and in the garage turntable. Pick yours in the lobby; the AI is dealt the rest in turn, so a full field never looks cloned.

The calendar

26 circuits.
Surveyed, not sketched.

Centerlines from public GPS traces, smoothed without shrinking the circuit. Banking laid onto the bends it belongs to. Elevation from satellite surface models, out to an 8 km horizon.

Unreal Engine 5

In the engine

The menu shell runs over a live AI demo race. Race view with HUD, sector timing, minimap and an optional racing line drawn from the server's per-car speed profile.

Architecture

Three parts,
one truth

Simulation logic stays isolated from presentation, so each piece can evolve on its own. The circuit you race is the circuit the server simulates, checked by CRC on both sides.

server/ · Rust

Authoritative server

240 Hz tokio loop. Physics, OBB collision against cars and baked barriers, race control, AI, force feedback, lap timing and records. /health /metrics

UDP
60 Hz
game-unreal/ · C++

Unreal client

Menus as C++ widget trees, cockpit built per car at runtime, TV director, synthesized audio, DirectInput wheels. Every car a telemetry puppet.

baked
levels
track-editor/ · Bevy

Track editor

Authors the 3D scene on a logical track; ats-dress, ats-groom and ats-export bake it into buffers Unreal builds a level from.

Collision that means it

Every armco, tyre wall, stand and building is baked into a walls sidecar. Nothing off the road is decorative.

Track limits

Four wheels past the curb band for 0.2 s strikes the lap. Cut the course and it's gone too.

Racing line

A quasi-steady-state speed profile per car from its grip, downforce, power and brakes.

Assists, host-controlled

ABS, traction control, auto gearbox, steering assist. The session host decides what's allowed; the server enforces it.

Cockpit

Wheel, dash and scene-captured mirrors built per car. Seat, horizon lock and head motion are yours to set.

Mod-friendly content

Cars are a car.toml plus a GLB. Tracks are YAML. Import commandlets do the rest; nothing in Unreal is hand-made.
